reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from the same paper directly supports all key premises: it reports formation of isolated Pt/Pd sites, charge transfer to Pt/Pd, stronger nitrobenzene interaction, and a yield increase from 44.4% to 93.9% upon alloying, with no misrepresentation.
premises: Alloying Co, Cu, Ni into PtPd forms a high-entropy alloy (HEA) that creates isolated Pt and Pd sites
Electron transfer occurs from the cheap metals (Co, Cu, Ni) to Pt and Pd in the HEA
This charge transfer makes Pt/Pd sites more electron-rich (nucleophilic)
The electron-rich, isolated Pt/Pd sites enhance nitrobenzene adsorption and activation
Enhanced adsorption/activation leads to significantly higher nitrobenzene hydrogenation activity
